section_1.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
section_1.content: Define a vector not just as a list of numbers, but as an entity possessing both magnitude and direction. Contrast this with 'scalars' (single numbers).
section_1.example: A drone flying: The speed (5 m/s) is a scalar, but the path (North-East at 5 m/s) is a vector.

section_2.title: Visualizing Vectors in 2D Space
section_2.content: Represent vectors as directed arrows on a Cartesian plane starting from the origin. Explain the coordinate representation (x, y).
section_2.example: An arrow starting at (0,0) and ending at (3,2). Visualize it as moving 3 units right and 2 units up.

section_3.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
section_3.content: Explain how to combine two vectors. Introduce the 'tip-to-tail' method where the tail of the second vector starts at the tip of the first.
section_3.example: A cat walks 2 meters East, then 3 meters North. The resultant vector is the straight line from the starting point to the final position.

section_4.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
section_4.content: Discuss what happens when you multiply a vector by a number. A scalar changes the magnitude (stretching/shrinking) and can reverse the direction if negative.
section_4.example: A robot arm extending: Multiplying the vector (1, 1) by a factor of 2 results in (2, 2), effectively doubling its reach.

section_5.title: Conclusion & Real-World Application
section_5.content: Summarize how these building blocks (addition/scaling) form the basis of Linear Algebra used in game physics, machine learning, and computer graphics.
section_5.example: In video games, thousands of tiny vectors are added together to calculate the movement of characters across a 3D landscape.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Map to right side of the screen
                x = 2.0 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_text = ["Vectors possess both magnitude and direction.", "Scalars are represented by single numbers.", "Think of vectors as directed paths."]
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: What is a Vector?", lecture_lines_text)
        
        # Define objects
        origin = Dot(point=np.array([2.0, 2.0, 0]), color=WHITE)
        target_point = Dot(point=self.grid["B4"], color=WHITE)
        vector = Arrow(start=origin.get_center(), end=target_point.get_center(), color="#FF5733", buff=0)
        label_v = Text("Vector V", font_size=24, color="#FF5733")
        label_v.next_to(target_point, UP, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Create(target_point), Create(origin))
        self.play(Create(vector), Write(label_v))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        # Pulsing effect for magnitude
        self.play(vector.animate.scale(1.2).set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(vector.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_color("#FF5733"), run_time=0.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
